title: Fix faux nightshift lighting lasting forever
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

When updating APCs, night shift does `set_nightshift(!nightshift_disabled)`. 
`nightshift_disabled` is only set to `TRUE` in the event the station is on red alert, meaning during a typical run, night shift would run its course, turn off, and then call `set_nightshift(!FALSE)` / `set_nightshift(TRUE)`.

Additionally, `tick` is not called after an event `end`s - meaning if the event failed to complete its `currentrun`, any unhandled APCs would stay in whatever state.

(I will note, this is realllllyyyy slow. Like, visually. It can only run about 12 APCs at a time before it pauses for next tick.)

changes.text: Night lighting actually goes away when it ends

title: The lightening: minor fix for lighting overlay hard deletes
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

fixes #98319

```
## REF SEARCH Found /datum/component/overlay_lighting [0x21058116] in list Datums -> /datum/spatial_grid_cell [0x21009cab] -> dynamic_light_sources (list).
## REF SEARCH Found /datum/component/overlay_lighting [0x21058116] in list Datums -> /datum/spatial_grid_cell [0x21009cac] -> dynamic_light_sources (list).
## TESTING: GC: -- [0x21058116] | /datum/component/overlay_lighting was unable to be GC'd -- (ref count of 4)
```

This is the rest of #97967. that got closed as a dupe of #97786, but #97786 only fixed part of it.

The component works out which grid cells to leave from its current range, so changing the range while it's lit leaves it in the cells only the old range reached. burning mobs hit this since the fire light shrinks as the stacks burn down. deleting the light then hard dels the component, and any lumcount read in those cells runtimes on it (`Cannot read null.current_holder`)

#97786 also left a few other ways to end up in the wrong cells:
- switching a light off without moving it kept it in its cells, so it still counted as light
- `set_light_range(0)` turned the light off without cleaning up
- the light picks its first holder before the component is listening, so moving that first holder (a light spawned on the floor, a mob's own light) never moved its cells
- a light taken out of a bag on the same tile it went in on stayed out of the grid

Now the component remembers the cells it registered in and leaves exactly those, clears them first on every re-register like #97967 did, re-registers when its range changes, cleans up when it's switched off, and grabs its first holder once it's listening. Range changes also update the holder's luminosity now, that used to stay at whatever range the light had when it got picked up or switched on. `set_power()` doesn't re-register anymore since nothing reads the stored power, and moving a lit light builds one cell list per step instead of two

Tested and verified to be dead for good now, stupid hard deletes

## Why It's Good For The Game

Hard dels are bad, and shadow walking and the other darkness checks now see lights where they actually are

changes.text: switched off lights no longer count as light for shadow walking and other darkness checks, and lights that move around count where they actually are

title: Adds a balloon warning when ventcrawling into pipes that arn't room temperature.
author: moocowswag
body:
## About The Pull Request


When entering pipes via ventcrawl do_after you will be alerted if the vent feels hot or cold (and in absence of an alert, room temperature)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b78d6cf-fd55-46f4-b67d-2633f40112eb

The way it is implemented should give you a warning near where you are already looking so you can easily react within the time it takes for the do_after to complete.

Breathability and pressure remain unknown until you subject yourself to the container. 

## Why It's Good For The Game
Its annoying to have to dance around in pipes waiting for life or atmos or whatever to tick to see if the gas mix is going to kill you, this eliminates the most obvious case of extreme temperatures which often results in long lasting damage or for slimes an instant death.

I thought about doing more cases for breathability and pressure but it would make the balloon alert too large....and to_chat warnings are too annoying to look at and diagnose if its something your controlled mob cares about within the timeframe of the do_after...especially when you could be getting hit while trying to ventcrawl.

That and its more intuitive to be able to tell the temperature of something's contents via initial contact than pressure or gas composition.



An alternative to this pr (or in addition to it) could be to add an alt-right click (or something) functionality to ventcrawlers to allow them to stick their head in to briefly sense contents without having to wait for something to tick or anything.

But I think that would have much more considerations of being able to fully discover if a pipenet is completely safe for you...currently the pr already appropriately telegraphs the main threat of entering a vent and arguably the only threat that should be telegraphed.

I could add more tells like "warm/hot/very hot" but im not sure if that would be too much?

I dont know if its qol or not...for most cases its qol because youre just saving time awkwardly spent dancing in a pipe, for slimes it could be considered balance since cold pipes are a stunlock into effectively an instant kill with no warning (although did we ever want that to begin with?)

title: Wounds for robotic limbs (ported from bubberstation and recoded)
author: Fghj240
body:
## About The Pull Request
_ew, the FURRY is porting stuff from a FURRY ERP server!!_

This PR adds wounds for robotic bodyparts, which takes code from skyrat, nova, and bubber. It does not add slash or pierce wounds, only burn and blunt ones, a lot of the mechanics were heavily adjusted including making them weaker overall. 

**Bleeding wounds** aren't coming (for now at least) because I think the idea of a wound just dealing damage over time to you is stupid and chip damage is especially annoying when you can't heal with medicine. Plus, it's a LOT of code and I don't even know if this is gonna get merged so I'm breaking it down.

**Burn wounds** are the metal heating up to a glow. The bodypart takes more damage like a normal burn wound, and you also glow a little while burned. Burns slowly raise your body temperature, but not that much. To fix them, you just have to lower your body temperature through any means or apply reagents onto yourself via touch or just spray yourself with an extinguisher or stand under a shower. Cooling yourself through reagent exposure causes thermal shock though, which deals mild amounts of brute damage based on the volume of the reagent applied. You can make your reagents more effective (and thus more damage efficient) by cooling them before splashing them onto you, or using a reagent with a higher specific heat value (#37691). Current that is only plasma and the one new cooling reagent just for this wound. Also, chilled coolant spray bottles are mapped into robotics.

In terms of effects, burn wounds cause damage vulnerability on the robotic limb, flavored as heated metal becoming more malleable. They also slowly raise body temperature, but not to the extent of them actually becoming deadly unless you have like 4+ critical burns. Because they can't get infected, they're a lot less dangerous than organic wounds and combined with the fact that they cal cool off on their own you might as well just ignore them. I didn't really want to make them slowly kill you over time though so whatever, at least they matter in combat. 

**Blunt wounds** cause oscillation in the wound which forces you to stop or grasp the limb in order to not be knocked down or drop your stuff every couple of seconds when it starts vibrating. It also disables the limb like normal, making interactions with that limb slower. T3 fractures disable a limb entirely. T1 blunt wounds can be fixed via rng every time you're hit in that body part with a blunt attack (percussive maintenance) or just with a screwdriver and a couple seconds. The T2 is fixed with a screwdriver and then welder, but the screw driver step has a failure chance if you're doing it on yourself so you can use bone gel instead to glue the bodypart internals instead of fastening them (there is no glue item in ss13 afaik) or crowbar the part open completely, which deals some brute and disables the limb but lets you fix it with a screwdriver guaranteed. The failure chance is mitigated by wearing a diagnostic hud, having someone else treat you, or scanning the wound with a wound scanner. The T3 wound can only be fixed by having a very high body temperature or a burn wound on the broken limb to make the metal more malleable, and then prying it back into place with a crowbar. That downgrades it to a T2 blunt wound, which then still needs to be fixed with a screwdriver and finally a welder.

As for the actual effects, they are very similar to organic wounds in order to make them easily intuitable. Head fractures cause fracture-derived brain trauma, leg fractures cause limping, and chest fractures don't cause bleeding when attacked but instead cause brief stagger and confusion.

In terms of code you can make reagent containers spawn with chems at a different temp now, I had to add that for chilled coolant spray.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Adds more depth to robotic bodyparts. The wounds aren't even that bad.

changes.text: Added burn and blunt wounds for robotic bodyparts
Added a new reagent, a coolant for robotic burns.
Added chilled coolant spray (for robotic burn wounds) to robotics
removed magic strings from bone repair surgery required states text

title: 3 positive quirks / some minor quirk changes
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

- Adds `Eccentric Correspondent`, 2 point positive quirk. Expands your mail list considerably to include items from any job, and then some. 
- Adds `Well Connected`, 6 point positive quirk. Grants you a discount on goodies and private orders from cargo, as well as on black market items. (And it has a sekret interaction as well)
- Adds `Shock Reflex`, 6 point positive quirk. Reduces the chance you get shocked when hacking vending machines or placing cables or the like. Does not effect chance to be shocked from bumping into shocked doors, for example.

- Removes some of the stranger mail goodies from a few quirks. 
   - Removed organ transport boxes from `Prosthetic Organ` and `Tin Man`
- Reduces chance of getting quirk mail from certain quirks that have stranger mail pools.
   - Affected quirks: Body Purist, Family Heirloom, Glass Jaw, Hemiplegic, Illiterate, Prosopagnosia, Pushover, Monochromatic, Pineapple hater, Pineapple Liker, Shifty Eyes, Vegetarian, Chipped, Freerunning, Jolly, Self Aware
- Increases chance of Gamer getting their mail

- Reduces quirk cost of throwing arm from 7 -> 5

## Why It's Good For The Game

- Quirks: A little more variety on the positive quirk front. Nothing super gamebreaking. 
   - `Eccentric Correspondent` allows people who love to pick up mail to gamble for wackier items. 
   - `Well Connected` is intended for people who have more "under-worldly" characters.

title: Tweals dynamic midround chances
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

The old formula for determining if we should spawn a midround was
```dm
	var/chance = 0
	var/num_antags = length(GLOB.current_living_antags)
	var/num_dead = length(GLOB.dead_player_list)
	var/num_alive = get_active_player_count(afk_check = TRUE)
	if(num_dead + num_alive <= 0)
		return 0

	chance += 100 - (200 * (num_dead / (num_alive + num_dead)))
	if(num_antags < 0)
		chance += 50

	return chance
```
But there's 3 notable errors here
1. `if(num_antags < 0)`. This never happens, for obvious reasons
2. `var/num_alive = get_active_player_count(afk_check = TRUE)` Default argument has `alive_check = FALSE`, meaning this gets dead players, meaning this is (in practice) `var/num_players`.
3. `length(GLOB.dead_player_list)`. If you disconnect after you die, or take a ghost role, you no longer count as dead. 

New formula:
```dm
	var/total_crew = 0
	var/dead_or_mia = 0
	for(var/datum/mind/crew_mind as anything in get_crewmember_minds())
		if(isnull(crew_mind.current) || crew_mind.current.stat <= HARD_CRIT)
			dead_or_mia += 1
		total_crew += 1

	var/chance = 100 - (300 * (dead_or_mia / total_crew))
	if(length(GLOB.current_living_antags) <= 0)
		chance += 50

	return chance
```
Notable changes:
- It now counts all crewmembers who are alive or dead, rather than all players who are alive or dead. This means every crewmember who is dead slightly reduces the chance for midrounds to spawn, even if the player disconnects or takes a ghost role. 
   - Why: Dead crewmembers is more indicative of the status of the crew than dead players - otherwise, there's a funny phenomenon where a player dies, takes an antag role, and then the chance of antag spawning *goes up*. Likewise, if a nuke team gets wiped out, the chance of antag spawning *goes down*, since there's now a lot of ghosts hanging around. 
- the +50% chance if there are no living antags is properly factored in.   
   - Why: Bugfix. We want dynamic to spawn at least one antag if possible.
- the chance to add antags hits 0% when half the crew is dead, rather than the entire crew. 
   - Why: Before it literally required 100% of the server be dead to have the chance to spawn an antag hit 0%. Raising it to 50% (of the crew being dead) gives the other half of the crew a chance to escape. 
    
Other changes:
- Midround rulesets that require ghosts get set to zero weight if there are no ghosts. This means instead of picking a ruleset -> picks a ghost ruleset -> nothing happens, it will pick a ruleset that can actually execute.
   - Why: Sometimes, dynamic will have a lot of rulesets it wants to execute, but no ghosts to execute them with. This change **heavily** prioritizes stuff like Mass Traitor under the assumption that it will make more ghosts (to use on ghost rulesets later on).
   
Potential changes:
- Each living antag should be tracked for activity. If a supermajority of antags are inactive, chance goes up. ("activity" meaning actively antagonizing, not connected and playing.)
   - Why: If there is 1 traitor who hasn't done anything for 30 minutes, dynamic should guarantee a spawn. 
- Deaths too early into the round don't count towards reduced antag chance
   - Why: Prevent roundstart suicides from affecting antag chances throughout the round, realistically only deaths to antags should count (though tracking such a thing is infeasible).
- Rather than using chance, keep a running counter that goes up and down in response to certain events (such as an antag or crewmember dying) - then spawn an antag only if over a threshold and reset
    - Why: Because it's a probability, and it's checked every 5 minutes, it's gonna happen eventually. Let's say 10 people are dead on a 50 player round. After 15 minutes, that's a ~78% chance to spawn an antag. This is kind of hard to account for when balancing dynamic, so the thought is we could tie it to concrete events or progression milestones. 
  
## Why It's Good For The Game

This formula was totally broken which probably made dynamic a bit more unpredictable than it should've been
I'm also not confident in what exactly fixing it will do to dynamic. I know for certain there will be less antags on average for rounds with a lot of dead people, though.

changes.text: Dynamic has a significantly higher chance of spawning antags if there are no antags alive
Dynamic no longer counts dead people as alive for the purpose of antag spawn chance
Dynamic math changed slightly. Fewer antags are spawned if a significant amount of the crew is dead, and observers who were never part of the crew no longer reduce the chance of spawning antags.

Dynamic rulesets that a require ghosts cannot be picked if there are no ghosts. This means midround rulesets like Traitors / Mass Traitors will be significantly more common when there are no observers.

title: Removes excess filters from all SM setups, standardizes them a bit well
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request Removes the extra filters from the SM output on every map. Standardizes waste output on all maps to a design similar to that of Icebox and Delta, with a pressure valve leading out to space and a temperature valve leading into waste. Example (Metastation) Also took the opportunity to do stuff like clean up pipe runs, relocate vents/scrubbers into more convenient / balanced places, etc ## Why It's Good For The Game About a year ago I would against this change - I considered it to be soul - I figured people could find a use out of the extra filters - I'm against over-simplifaction / over-optimization of the default setup However over the past year I've come around on the idea - I still think it's soul, but it really does serve no purpose - I can't think of a use for them at all. Most people who add extra filters to speed up the rate that which it pumps air through rip them all up regardless. - I don't feel like removing them simplifies or optimizes the default setup in a major way And the benefits of doing it... - Easier for newer players. - For them, it's not at all obvious why the other filters even exist. - Nor is it obvious that failing to turn the three extra filters to "enabled, no filter" is *required* to avoid a later disaster. - Their main purpose ends up being a subtle way for the AI to sabotage the SM, which is something most newer players won't really know to check. - Clears up space, either for in round changes or mapping. (I used some of the extra space to standardize the setups a bit.) And why I standardized the outputs - I recognize that maps having unique facets gives them something that differentiates them (which is cool and good) but I'm on record stating the SM is like *the only* thing that shouldn't have major differences, due to its ability to explode and kill the round. (Birdshot proved that.) - Using the more niche components on a roundstart setup also helps teach people what they can be used for, which is neat.

author: KOCMODECAHTHUK
body: ## Описание изменений Добавляет механики: - Жажду и Вес и перегруз. Добавлена жажда для основных рас, которые теперь нуждаются в её утолении. - Напитки пополняют жажду, у разных реагентов свои значения утоления жажды. - В наборы выживания добавлены питательный батончик и бутылка воды; обновлено самообследование состояния. Вес и перегруз. Система переноса веса: - Теперь у предметов есть масса. - У контейнеров - процентное снижение веса (рюкзак -30%, сумка -25%, дафл -15%, пояс -50%, MODsuit −50%, РПЭД/мешки для руды и листов, блюспейс-контейнеры). - 100u реагента = 1 кг, дозы (таблетки, патчи) почти невесомы, материалы весят по штукам. - Персонажи на плече весят вдвое меньше собственной массы. (У человека/гуманоида по умолчанию вес 60кг) Перегруз: - Максимальный переносимый вес 50кг, который может снижаться от потребностей персонажа. - Вплоть до 120% от максимума персонаж падает, - Голод и жажда снижают грузоподъёмность. - Перегруз ускоряет расход еды и воды при ходьбе (до ×2.5). Изменены HUD - Полоски голода и жажды заменены круговыми индикаторами. - Добавлен индикатор перегруза и подсказки при наведении. ## Причина создания ПР / Почему это хорошо для игры Еда без воды была неполной механикой выживания: теперь есть жажда. Вес делает выбор снаряжения более осмысленным и доходить к нему с умом: Теперь быть манчкином неудобно, а контейнеры и броня влияют по-разному. Голод, жажда и вес связаны: перегруженный и голодный персонаж быстрее выдыхается, поэтому есть смысл брать воду и еду. ## Демонстрация изменений / Тестирование

title: Insulated dead bodies cool down instead of staying hot forever
author: AitorLogedo
body:
## About The Pull Request

Dead humans wearing anything that insulates against cold (sec gear, winter coats, etc) never cool down after burning.

#78508 reported corpses never cooling down and #78572 fixed it in `/mob/living/carbon/handle_environment`, but humans override `handle_environment` without calling the parent and use the species temperature code instead, so that fix only ever worked for monkeys, aliens and other carbons. A naked human corpse still cools down on its own through the skin code, which is probably why it looked fixed.

With insulation it gets stuck: every tick the room takes some heat from the skin, then the core gives it right back because core to skin transfer is multiplied by `(1 + thermal_protection)` and capped at the difference. A dead core doesn't stabilize, so it never goes down and the body stays hot forever, taking heat damage the whole time until it husks.

Now dead humans cool their skin and core towards the room temperature the same way #78572 does for other carbons, without insulation. Living mobs aren't touched.

## Why It's Good For The Game

A corpse in a vest shouldn't stay at 800K for 15 minutes and husk itself while medbay is trying to fix it.

## Testing

Unit test that burns humans with 2 fire stacks, ticks the fire and Life() by hand and resets the room air every tick:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| dead, security outfit, time under 340K after the fire is out | never, 831K after 15 minutes | 84 seconds |
| dead, winter coat | never, 426K after 15 minutes | 78 seconds |
| dead, naked | 74 seconds | 38 seconds |
| dead security officer burned with 2 stacks, real damage | 600 burn, husked | 168 burn, not husked |
| alive, any outfit | 46 to 94 seconds | same |

changes.text: Dead bodies wearing insulating clothes cool down after burning instead of staying hot and husking.

title: Implements baking navigational data into turf, and uses this for a DLL-based A* implementation (With Multi-Z support)
author: CabinetOnFire
body: ## About The Pull Request Pathfinding has always been a difficult thing to deal with in our game. In particular when it has to take in account things like directional windows (which makes traditional 1/0 checks less feasible), and conditional blockers (things with passability, doors with access, etc). To combat this, this PR has two major changes: First of all, there is now a "navmap" subsystem, and each turf stores its passability on it (as much as it can) It keeps track of the following: - Whether its nav data is baked. - Whether the turf is simulated or unsimulated space. - Ground and flying passability for each horizontal direction. - Direct vertical passability for flying movers. - Which outgoing edges have conditional blockers. - The conditional blockers associated with each outgoing edge. Conditional blockers are stored once and evaluated only when a path actually needs them. This avoids repeatedly scanning every atom on a turf during pathfinding. Mobs are never baked into the navmap; they remain live movement-time obstructions. The navmap is maintained by SSnavmap. Dirty turfs and their relevant neighbors are queued for asynchronous rebaking. Changes to vertical neighbors also invalidate dependent openspace edges, so fallability changes do not leave stale navigation data behind. Automatic dirtying is enabled for the station and mining z-levels. Other levels can be baked lazily or explicitly prebaked. Individual updates are sent to the native cache as needed, while full z-level prebakes are published in bulk. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eeddb38a-f0b6-4dfc-9834-711e16e76167 Secondly, by default we now use a rust-g DLL (with a dm backup) to run through this pathfinding. The native cache receives: - Packed turf passability data. - Bulk z-level updates. - Z-level topology and layer information. - Registered cross-z navigation links. - The native A* implementation avoids BYOND calls for unconditional edges and only calls back into DM for conditional blockers or mover-dependent link checks. Native jobs can run synchronously or in resumable slices of roughly 5 ms. There is also a native-compatible DM A* fallback. It is used automatically when the DLL is unavailable and can be forced for debugging. The fallback uses the same packed navmap data, live conditional checks, diagonal corner rules, simulated-turf handling, path limits, and movement costs as the native implementation. Both implementations support: - Ground and flying movement. - Diagonal handling. - Maximum search distance. - Minimum target distance. - Avoided turfs. - Maximum total path cost. - Start-tile skipping. - Conditional pass flags and access checks. essentially the same as JPS (path cost is new tho) Repo for the DLL: https://github.com/CabinetOnFire/navmap-pathfinder I'll also give some more in-depth performance numbers once I can set up some test cases. but the difference is huge. **Multi-Z** also added support for Multi-z pathfinding. To do this there is also a concept known as z-level topology, which tracks whether z-levels are connected. flying movers can use direct vertical edges when both turfs allow the appropriate zPassIn/zPassOut transition. Ground movers can use registered navigation links such as ladders and stairs Navigation links essentially are abstract connections between two turfs with a set of instructions how to move between those turfs. e.g. ladders will say "I move you from this turf to the turf above, if you want to do it you need to interact with the ladder" Navigation links have: - Source and destination turfs. - A traversal cost. - Live eligibility checks. - Native and DM fallback support. - Actual traversal callbacks, so pathfinding uses the same ladder or stair behavior as normal gameplay. Unreachable z-level groups are rejected before starting an expensive search Some additional fixes/changes - Navmap pathfinding can repath due to changing target now - Bots now respond more reliably to summons - Bot paths can now go further than 25 tiles ## Why It's Good For The Game we use a looot of server time on pathfinding, and we only really used it for bots. This should lower that by quite a bit.

changes.text: Pathfinding now makes use of a more optimized rust-g A* algorithm
Bots now should reliably be summonable

title: Optimize pressure damage calculation by only updating when equipment or bodyparts change (70% of our `get_bodypart` calls)
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request Currently ever life tick, we run `calculate_affecting_pressure` to see the effective pressure a mob is experiencing at that very moment This proc checks worn equpiment to see if it protects from pressure damage. It also checks if the mob is missing limbs (as missing limbs don't need protection) Unsurprisingly checking all limbs and all equipment every life tick is a little wasteful. In fact this is responsible for like 70% of our remaining `get_bodypart` calls on its own I made it state based. Adding and removing bodyparts adds or removes relevant flags, and equipping and unequipping items does as well (this is handled the same place obscuring is handled, since they're very very similar.) Only other change I had to do was adding a proc for enabling / disabling item coverage, so we could react to it and update. That way if your firesuit is ripped it stops protecting you, or whatever.

title: Removes CatwalkStation
author: san7890
body: ## About The Pull Request Removes Catwalk Station from the game. ## Why It's Good For The Game There are a few metrics that stick out in my mind that need to be elaborated on: --- ### Codebase The last catwalk-specific fix (related to CI) was in #97886 (25b1dbc26bdb8eeddf64ee3c3d1ee44a9f6a94f7) - End of September 2026 The last concrete actual map specific to catwalk fix was in #97281 (0992ec02722bbb855ff38172315c16c28f4d2b61) - End of July 2026 The last actual mapped feature for catwalk was in #94741 (2fb903b55e28fecd119c10bdaed6edcb058d5be0) - End of January 2026 In fact, most of the features (from what I can tell), were a work of labor from @loganuk. The most recent feature feature I can find that was not done by this mapper was in #91650 (8fee5623b9c733e9e45a4f2d713a4ea129991d80) - June-July 2025 On a precursory view, a majority of updates to Catwalk have been "Mega Map Reworks", or major changes to all maps in relation to a new mapping norm or the encoding of a feature. In order to understand just how low frequency these are, I welcome you to look at the PRs labelled with the [Map Edit Tag](https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/pulls?q=is%3Apr+state%3Aclosed+label%3A%22Map+Edit%22). Pretty much everything (except Nebula) has had several PRs minor tweaks/fixes or revamps from several different mappers with a more dense frequency over a much more recent timespan. I understand this to be signal that no more than a few people are actively interested in working on this map. --- ### Adminbase I can not speak for the current opinions of the headmins or wider admin base, and a poll might be worth conducting if you really want the answer here. They are welcome to opine, as always. This is the current settings, from [the config found here](https://github.com/tgstation-operations/server-config/blob/main/maps.txt): ```txt map catwalkstation minplayers 25 votable feedbacklink https://forums.tgstation13.org/viewtopic.php?p=745280 endmap ``` I will give a very recent anecdote in my position of this capacity for the time being: On Manuel, where a vote of Catwalk went through, and I could see the readied player count fall to about 30% of online players (about 15 of 50) with 2 minutes to go until the round started, a far cry from the typical 50-60% you would expect on that server in recent weeks. Since I was strongly worried about a sudden precipitous drop in population on Manuel, I suspended the start and changed it to a different map (based on a vote). This was concurred on by another admin online at the time in the capacity that admins have the authority to make the game fun, and then it got me thinking about my other official capacities. I sustained pop, but the thought continued to linger in my mind. That's ultimately what led to this being proposed. --- ### Playerbase There have not been any recent polls assessing player popularity of maps conducted, but I believe that there not an overwhelming outpouring of support for this map for several reasons. A poll might be worth conducting if a definitive answer is desired here, but I do not know if this is necessary at the moment. Here are some stats that I've sourced from https://scrubbier.papamichael.dev/stats . I am only counting Manuel as that can be reasonably interpreted as being the most consistently active server over the last 90 day span: In the last 90 days, Catwalk Station has been ran on 2% of all low-pop rounds (88% of Overall Manuel Shifts; <25 pop). [link](https://scrubbier.papamichael.dev/stats?server=manuel&window=90&pop=lo) In the last 90 days, Catwalk Station has been ran on **0%** of all high-pop rounds (12% of Overall Manuel Shifts; >= 25 pop) [link](https://scrubbier.papamichael.dev/stats?server=manuel&window=90&pop=hi) The second finding is especially interesting when you realize that _Catwalk is designed to be ran at a minimum of 25 players per the config_! I believe this as a strong signal that people (or whatever the map vote weighting is doing) on a previous higher population shift is causing Catwalk to pass on higher population shifts, and then the very next round has a high precipitous downfall in players. This isn't entirely founded, but is plausible based on my own personal experience. It's a very disturbing trend for people to vote for a map with a chunk of the server leaving in protest to dip it below the voting point. It's not present in any other map, as Nebula (minpop 35) seems to have a decent share of being voted in highpop and retaining it's share in highpop instead of instantly cratering in the same pattern Catwalk appears to be following. I do not like the pattern of having a "poison" map in the rotation in this manner. The reaction is also a reasonable demonstration of general sentiment (why play a game if you aren't having fun?). I do not see any way to resolve this beyond the measure proposed in this PR. ## In Summary Based on these metrics, I do not think it is fair to: A) Contributors to be responsible for mapping in their features into this map with how little it gets played. B) Server operators and administrators to have to put up with this map cratering population during any active seeding sessions (as changing it in configuration would be a unilateral death sentence for this map anyways, and they are too polite to the maptainers and desires of this repository to do that). C) Players to have to be subject to this map being ran in an adverse manner as it appears to be completely subversive to any principle of _voluntas populi_. I suppose another question might be "what map will replace Catwalk?". The truthful answer is, I don't think we need more than 6 maps, especially looking at the above statistics. We can bring back Pubby or something but this shouldn't be a prerequisite for removing this map. I don't think there is much alternative that satisfies all three concerned parties. _Stats accurate to the time the PR was published._

title: Doubles the potency of synthflesh
author: TheRyeGuyWhoWillNowDie
body:
## About The Pull Request

Doubles the healing of synthflesh from (base purity) 1.25 brute/burn per unit to 2.5 brute/burn per unit. Tox damage remains proportional (i.e it's also doubled), also doesn't change unhusking threshold. 

## Why It's Good For The Game

Long ago, Synthflesh was THE medical healing chem. Back then, you could put chems in fire extinguishers too so you could fill a fire extinguisher with synthflesh and spray it onto people to basically aheal them. Many many years have passed since then and synthflesh has been gutted over and over. Fermichem made it extremely tedious to make and impurity massively reduced its healing potential, and cobbychem added tox damage to it as 'recoil' and also massively reduced its raw healing. These days, synthflesh is used for the sole and exclusive purpose of being that stuff you buy from the med-vendor to dehusk people and it's been that way for more than five years.

Doubling the potency of synthflesh makes it much, much more efficient for its 'intended' healing purpose, that being a fast-track to avoid having to do surgery on people just barely above the 180 damage revival threshold. Not in the sense of making it an overpowered general healer (as tox damage remains proportional, and 1u of real medicines heal 10x as much as 1u of synthflesh) but simply in reducing the amount you have to use per patient. Due to mechanics like bio armor on jumpsuits reducing synthflesh's healing potential even more, people with as little as 240 damage take north of 100 units of 100% pure synthflesh to get to under 180 damage, making a bluespace beaker of the stuff only good for as little as two uses. Doubling the healing potential might still not even be good enough for it to be worth making, but it's a start and will hopefully encourage people to make this stuff again.

title: Makes radiation a bit deadlier
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request 1. Adds a form of limited radiation spreading. - Individuals irradiated from a powerful primary source (such as the Supermatter) will spread their radiation to nearby mobs. - This is visually denoted by the glow around spreaders being slightly brighter. - It can also be detected via geiger counter. - Standing underneath a shower prevents spreaders from spreading radiation. - However, individuals irradiated from secondary sources (such as someone irradiated from the Supermatter) or from minor primary sources (like chemicals or uranium) will not spread their radiation. 2. Being irradiated for a moderate amount of time will irradiate your internal organs. - Irradiated organs take organ damage over time and cause additional tox damage. - These organs will have special text in the health analyzer pointing them out. - This is also separate from "standard" radiation, i.e. you can have irradiated organs but not be glowing green. - Non-organic organs will not have radiation spread to them. - Currently, if you get some irradiated cyber lungs and put them in a normal human, there is no effect at all. This might change though. - If an organ is irradiated while "in world" and placed into a mob, it would have the same negative effects. - Radiation healing chemicals such as Pentetic Acid will heal organ damage caused by irradiation. - Additionally, upon fully healing an irradiated organ, the chem un-irradiates the organ. 3. Plasmamen, Androids, and similarly immune mobs can be irradiated again - though are still immune to its effects. - This allows Plasmamen to spread radiation intentionally via the spread mechanic above like back in the day. - Showers and other methods of direct decontamination are the only way to clean these species of radiation (tox chems won't work). - Slimepeople are similarly reliant on showers instead of antirad chems. 4. Standing underneath a shower *very slowly* reverses irradiation, rather than only pausing it. 5. Radioactive chems will now irradiate organs. (Breathing uranium irradiates the lungs, eating uranium irradiates the stomach, injecting uranium irradiates the liver.) 5. Misc. Changes - Seiver numbers have been tweaked, reducing the radiation tox healing per tick from 45(!!) to 10. - Space cleaner now deals tox tamage per tick, though a minor amount. It can also rarely clean your organs squeaky clean. *Pictured: advanced health analyzer showing organ irradiation status.* ## Why It's Good For The Game Ever since radiation's changes years ago many have commented that radiation is now a pretty lackluster threat, and I echo some of these thoughts. So I wanted to address some of it while keeping it in line with the original design document proposed all those years ago. - Irradiated organs makes persistent radiation more of a hazard and encourages use of specialty anti-rad medical over any generic toxins healer. Treatment is still intuitive: Heal toxloss, fix organs. Even if a newer player if confused how to fix radioactive organs, they can always outright replace them. - Limited radiation spreading encourages quarantining and wearing proper protective equipment. Medbay will occasionally need to procure rad suits to deal with big problems, but failing to get a radsuit doesn't result in a death spiral.

changes.text: Individuals irradiated from a powerful primary source (such as the Supermatter) will spread radiation around them. This is denoted by their radiation glow being brighter than normal. Importantly, this will not cascade further, meaning any individual irradiated from them will NOT spread it further.
Plasmamen, Androids, and other radiation immune species can be irradiated once again, though are still immune to the effects. Only methods of direct decontamination (like showering) will clear it.
Slimepeople can now properly be affected by radiation. Like Plasmamen, it can only be cleared via direct decontamination.
Showers will now heal irradiation very slowly in addition to pausing the negative effects.

Untreated irradiation will eventually spread to your internal organs, causing organ damage and further complications. While it can spread to robotic organs, this has no effect (for now). And yes, inserting an irradiated organ into an otherwise clean patient will cause the radiation to spread to the body over time.
Anti-rad medication such as Pentetic Acid now reverses organ damage caused by irradiation (and eventually clears irradiated organs entirely) - so long as the affected organ hasn't failed entirely.
Radioactive chemicals like Uranium can now directly irradiate organs - for example, breathing radioactive smoke may irradiate your lungs.
Radiation has seen a few changes if you couldn't tell. Report any issues like mobs experiencing negative effects from irradiation when they otherwise shouldn't be.
